A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DynMoE work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original DynMoE experiments on DomainBed, GLUE, and vision-language benchmarks, alongside routing analyses, ablations, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds vision training experiments, adaptive-routing comparisons, method ablations, and runtime analyses.

M1.justification: The core top-any router, expert addition/removal procedure, and original auxiliary loss remain unchanged. Section 8.4 adds alternative expert initialization procedures using averaging, weighted averaging, or the most activated expert. Additional loss combinations, including DynMoE-B in Table 20, extend the method through optional variants.

E1.justification: v4 adds TinyImageNet classification fine-tuning, CIFAR-10 pretraining, and ImageNet training from scratch (Tables 18–20). This substantially extends vision coverage beyond the original DomainBed domain-generalization experiments. The original language and vision-language benchmark coverage is retained.

E2.justification: v4 adds an evaluated adaptive top-p comparator with p=0.4 (Table 17), Dense-LLaVA in the runtime comparison, and top-1 timing controls. The efficiency baseline also changes from MoE-LLaVA using DynMoE's dispatcher to DeepSpeed's top-2 implementation. Existing main accuracy comparators remain.

E3.justification: The runtime evaluation adds first-token latency, wall-clock and component timings, exclusion of the initial allocation sample, and forced-top-1 controls. New vision experiments introduce separate training configurations, including 200-epoch ImageNet training with specified MoE layers and batch sizes. Original accuracy protocols are largely retained; the revised efficiency captions alone do not establish that retained FLOP measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's fixed-k and auxiliary-loss comparisons, v4 examines load-balancing/efficiency-loss combinations and their activation patterns (Tables 13–16), expert initialization strategies, routing overhead under matched top-1 activation, and equal versus score-weighted output aggregation (Table 23). These address several previously untested design choices and efficiency mechanisms.

E5.justification: v4 first supplies per-task ± uncertainty terms throughout the retained GLUE comparison in Table 11 and specifies five-trial averaging for Table 4. Both versions already state three random seeds for language and vision experiments, so increased seed counts are not established. The statistic represented by ± remains undefined.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive results in Tables 13–23 and Figure 24 while retaining the original main accuracy means. StableLM throughput changes from 26 versus 19 to 30 versus 27 tokens/second for DynMoE versus MoE-LLaVA under revised implementation settings, not a demonstrated same-setting improvement. Qwen/Phi-2 throughput entries disappear; their FLOP, MAC, and memory values remain in Table 24.

T1.justification: The mathematical development in Equations (1)–(8) is retained, with no new substantive derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof. The stated orientation of Wg is edited as a notation adjustment, and Algorithm 1 is relocated unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain automatic selection of expert counts and per-token activations, competitive performance across vision/language/vision-language tasks, and efficiency without extensive hyperparameter search. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these core scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations of load-balancing versus sparsity, initialization strategies, aggregation weights, and routing overhead. It acknowledges inefficient routing and suggests optimized kernels. The memory limitation remains in Section 4.4, but the conclusion removes v2's explicit larger-model evaluation limitation. The broad preference for W-Average also needs qualification because Table 19 favors Average initialization.

D1.justification: v4 adds localized reproducibility details for new experiments, particularly ImageNet optimizer settings, learning schedule, MoE placement, hardware, batch sizes, and timing configurations. Existing Appendix settings and Table 5 remain. The repository link is unchanged, while the explicit statement promising Tutel and DeepSpeed-MoE implementations is omitted; this does not establish that implementations were withdrawn.

R1.justification: Related work now discusses Huang et al.'s top-p routing and Yang et al.'s XMoE, distinguishing their hyperparameter or dense-training requirements. References supporting dynamic networks, layer skipping, additional losses, and new datasets are added. This is a focused expansion of positioning rather than a wholesale revision.

P1.justification: Most of the original narrative is preserved. Changes include localized prose edits, a rewritten conclusion, a subdivided experimental appendix, relocation of Algorithm 1 to Appendix 7, acknowledgments, and updated author/header and citation formatting. The additional experiments account for much of the new prose.

P2.justification: v4 adopts the ICLR layout, substantially resizes and redistributes existing displays, adds Tables 13–23 and Figure 24, and redesigns the main efficiency table. The earlier FLOP/MAC/memory comparison moves to Table 24 without its throughput column. Figures 1–23 retain their artwork despite relocation and resizing.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens validation of the central efficiency and routing claims. Native DeepSpeed comparisons and forced-top-1 controls expose routing overhead that v2's shared-dispatch comparison did not isolate. The adaptive top-p comparator and aggregation/initialization ablations address important validation gaps, while GLUE uncertainty reporting improves transparency. These gains outweigh narrower losses in throughput coverage and the removed larger-model caveat. Reporting weaknesses remain, including undefined ± terms and Table 14's unexplained activation frequency of 1.29.
